statusNote: This IPEDS entity is the flagship/headquarters campus of Keiser University, a private nonprofit university system with numerous branch campuses across Florida and abroad. The institution has been led continuously since its 1977 founding (as The Keiser School, becoming Keiser University in 2006) by co-founder Dr. Arthur Keiser, whose title shifted from President to Chancellor & CEO by 2016. Below Keiser, a separate 'President' role was created circa 2016 to run day-to-day operations of the flagship campus (first Gary Vonk, later others including Ryan Sagers as President of the Fort Lauderdale and Graduate School campuses); those campus-level presidents turn over more frequently and are not well documented for succession purposes, so they are omitted here in favor of the system's top (Chancellor) leader, which is the more relevant role for search-firm tracking. Legal nonprofit parent is Everglades College, Inc. (no formal university 'system' name).

leaders.notes: Co-founded the institution in 1977 as The Keiser School; it became Keiser College in 1986 and Keiser University in 2006. Held the title of President/CEO for most of that span, then shifted to Chancellor & CEO by 2016 as a separate flagship-campus President role was created underneath him. Still serving as Chancellor; has faced federal scrutiny (House Education Committee probe, 2022) over compensation drawn from the nonprofit Everglades College, Inc.
27th president of La Salle and the first alumnus of the university to hold the office; resigned in 1998 and returned to teaching, later chairing the Psychology Department until his death in 2016.
Emerged from the Board of Trustees to fill a one-year vacancy; first non-Christian-Brother to hold the presidency in La Salle's 135-year history at that time.

leaders.nextRole: Director, University Honors Program / President Emeritus (faculty)
leaders.notes: 28th president; became president of Christian Brothers University in 1994 before returning to lead his alma mater La Salle from 1999-2014. Stepped down in 2014 but stayed on as a religion professor and later directed the Honors Program.

Veteran higher-ed leader who had previously been the first lay president of Mount Aloysius College; bridged La Salle's leadership gap and helped run the search that led to Colleen Hanycz's appointment.
29th president; first female and first lay (non-interim) president in La Salle's history. Left in 2021 to become the 35th president of Xavier University.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President (previously CFO, Archdiocese of Philadelphia)
leaders.notes: La Salle alumnus ('85) who joined the Executive Cabinet as EVP in January 2021 and assumed interim presidential duties June 1, 2021, until Daniel Allen took over in 2022.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President for Advancement and External Relations
leaders.notes: 30th president, began April 18, 2022; career fundraiser in Catholic/Lasallian higher ed with prior stops at Lewis University and University of Chicago. Currently serving.

statusNote: Lamar University became part of the Texas State University System on September 1, 1995 after the Lamar University System (its own separate system) was dissolved by state legislation.

leaders.notes: Became president February 26, 1993; presided over Lamar's 1995 transition from its own Lamar University System into the Texas State University System. Resigned in March 1998; details of his prior and subsequent career were not found in available sources.
Historian who had led Stephen F. Austin State University for 14 years before coming out of retirement to serve as Lamar's interim president May 1998-1999, bridging the gap to James Simmons.

leaders.priorTitle: Interim Executive Director of Advancement (rose through faculty/dean ranks at Lamar)
leaders.notes: A Lamar 'lifer' who joined as a music instructor in 1970 and rose through department chair and dean of fine arts before becoming president in 1999. Resigned the presidency in 2013 to return to teaching music; named President Emeritus by the Texas State University System Board of Regents.

Joined Lamar in July 2013; was a finalist for the Southern Illinois University Carbondale chancellorship in 2020 before withdrawing. Announced retirement from Lamar in January 2021 and became the 19th president of Oklahoma City University that July.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: 16th president, took office July 2021, formally invested that November. Longtime Austin Peay State University administrator (dean of Science and Mathematics, physics department chair) before Marshall and then Lamar. Currently serving.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President and Director, Bunting Institute
leaders.nextRole: President, Walmart Foundation (later President, Suffolk University 2015-16)
leaders.notes: Led Lesley for 22 years, growing it from roughly 2,000 to over 10,000 students and from a college to a university with a nationally recognized teacher-education program. Former civil rights attorney and White House Deputy Counsel. Went on to lead the Walmart Foundation, then briefly served as Suffolk University's president (2015-16) before resigning amid a board dispute.

Selected unanimously by trustees in February 2007; served nine years and retired June 30, 2016. Earlier in his career was provost at Mansfield University (PA) and a planning official in the Vermont State Colleges system.

Lesley's sixth president, began July 1, 2016; announced June 19, 2018 he would step down effective August 31, 2018 citing personal health issues. Moved almost immediately into a healthcare executive role at Mass General Brigham.

Career interim-leadership specialist (prior interim roles at Wentworth Institute of Technology, University of New Orleans, University of Louisiana System, Union Institute & University); took over at Lesley effective September 1, 2018 and handed off to Janet Steinmayer in 2019.

Lesley's seventh president; former corporate lawyer (TWA general counsel) and hospitality-industry CEO (Centerplate) before running Mitchell College and then Lesley. Announced April 2026 she would step down effective June 30, 2026; her tenure's final months included a faculty strike (April 2026).

leaders.priorTitle: Chief Operations Officer (previously Interim Chief Information Officer)
leaders.notes: Named interim president effective July 1, 2026 following Steinmayer's departure; joined Lesley in 2020 and previously held senior technology/operations roles at Boston University, Olin College of Engineering, and Mitchell College. Currently serving.
